flagged.evidence: The definition calls the open star “the union of the relative interiors of simplices in \(\operatorname{St}_K(\sigma)\),” while defining \(\operatorname{St}_K(\sigma)=\{\tau:\sigma\cup\tau\in K\}\). For the path with edges \(\{v,w\},\{w,z\}\) and \(\sigma=\{v\}\), this set of simplices is \(\{\varnothing,\{v\},\{w\},\{v,w\}\}\), so the stated union is the closed edge \(|\{v,w\}|\). It is not open in the realization of the path, since every neighborhood of \(w\) meets the interior of \(|\{w,z\}|\). The standard open star instead takes interiors of cofaces containing \(\sigma\).

Step 1.1 says “Every simplex of \(K\) lies in exactly one summand \(K_\alpha\).” But the scoped abstract-complex definition requires \(\varnothing\in K_\alpha\) for every summand, so the empty simplex is shared whenever there is more than one summand. The chain-group decomposition only needs the corrected statement for nonempty simplices, since \(C_n\) is generated by them for \(n\ge0\).
